items.title: Ucuz kıyafetin bedeli
items.text: A shirt that costs very little looks like a good deal. The problem is what happens after the third wash. Cheap clothes are made from thin material and the stitching is done quickly, so they lose their shape and the colors fade. A buyer who pays a small amount four times a year has spent more than a buyer who paid a larger amount once. This is not new information, but it is easy to forget in a shop. There is also the question of who made the shirt and for what pay. Some companies now publish where their factories are, which at least makes the question possible to ask. The best advice is old and boring: buy less, buy better, and keep the receipt. It is boring because it works.

questions.q: What happens to cheap clothes after washing?
options: They lose their shape and fade
questions.note: "They lose their shape and the colors fade."

questions.q: What is the writer's point about cost?
options: Buying cheap four times costs more
questions.note: "A buyer who pays a small amount four times a year has spent more."

questions.q: What do some companies now publish?
questions.note: "Some companies now publish where their factories are."

questions.q: What is the writer's advice?
questions.note: "Buy less, buy better, and keep the receipt."

questions.q: Why does the writer call the advice boring?
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Kendi ekmeğini yapmak
items.titleEn: The Man Who Bakes at Five
items.text: Rifat is sixty-one and he has made bread every morning for nine years. He starts at five and finishes at half past seven, before most of his street is awake. He is not a baker. He worked in an office for thirty years and he never cooked anything until he retired. The first year the bread was terrible. His wife ate it without complaining, which he says was the reason he continued. Now he gives most of it away. Two neighbors leave a cloth bag on his door handle and collect it later. He has never taken money for a loaf and he becomes uncomfortable when anybody suggests it. When people ask why he does it, he says the honest answer is that he needed a reason to get up.

questions.q: When does Rifat finish?
questions.note: "He starts at five and finishes at half past seven."

questions.q: What did he do before?
questions.note: "He worked in an office for thirty years."

questions.q: Why did he continue after the first year?
options: His wife ate the bread without complaining
He had nothing else to do
questions.note: "His wife ate it without complaining, which he says was the reason he continued."

questions.q: How do the neighbors collect the bread?
options: They leave a bag on his door handle
questions.note: "Two neighbors leave a cloth bag on his door handle."

questions.q: What is his honest reason?
options: He needed a reason to get up
He wanted to learn a skill
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Sınıfta telefon yasağı
items.text: A school in the north of the country took every phone away at the door for one year and then measured what happened. Test results improved slightly, which is what the headmaster expected. What surprised him was the noise. The corridors between lessons became loud again. Students who had spent every break looking down were now talking, arguing and playing. Several teachers said it felt like a school from twenty years ago. There were costs too. Parents could not reach their children during the day, and some were unhappy about that. A few students said they felt lonely without the group conversations they were used to. The school decided to continue but to allow phones at lunch. The headmaster says the lesson is not that phones are evil; it is that a rule with no exceptions is easier to keep than one with many.

questions.q: What did the headmaster expect?
questions.note: "Test results improved slightly, which is what the headmaster expected."

questions.q: What surprised him?
questions.note: "What surprised him was the noise."

questions.q: What was one cost of the rule?
options: Parents could not reach their children
questions.note: "Parents could not reach their children during the day."

questions.q: What did the school finally decide?
options: Continue but allow phones at lunch
questions.note: "The school decided to continue but to allow phones at lunch."

questions.q: What does the headmaster say the lesson is?
options: A rule with no exceptions is easier to keep
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Kiraya çıkan ilk ev
items.text: Ozge moved into her first flat at twenty-three and made every mistake that people make. She signed the contract without reading the part about repairs. She paid for three months in advance because the owner said it would be safer, which it was, for him. She did not take photographs of the walls when she arrived, so when she left there was an argument about marks that were already there. None of these mistakes were expensive on their own, but together they cost her about two months of rent. She now tells younger friends the same four things: read the repair section, never pay more than one month in advance, photograph everything on the first day, and write down the meter readings. She says the advice is dull and nobody follows it until the first time it costs them something.

questions.q: What did Ozge not read?
questions.note: "She signed the contract without reading the part about repairs."

questions.q: Why did she pay three months in advance?
options: The owner said it would be safer
questions.note: "Because the owner said it would be safer."

questions.q: What was the argument about when she left?
questions.note: "There was an argument about marks that were already there."

questions.q: How much did the mistakes cost her?
questions.note: "Together they cost her about two months of rent."

questions.q: What does she say about her advice?
options: Nobody follows it until it costs them
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Konuşamayan iyi öğrenci
items.titleEn: Good at Grammar, Silent in Class
items.text: Baran was the best student in his English class on paper. He knew the tenses better than the teacher sometimes did, and his written work was almost perfect. In conversation he said almost nothing. When the teacher asked him a direct question he answered in three words and looked down. The teacher first thought he was shy, but Baran explained that the problem was different. He said he could hear the mistakes in his own speech before the words left his mouth, and stopping felt safer than being wrong in front of people. The teacher changed one thing. Instead of asking questions to the whole room, she put students in pairs for five minutes at the start of every lesson. Baran still hated the first week. By the sixth week he was the loudest person in his pair. His writing has not improved at all, and nobody minds.

questions.q: What was Baran good at?
questions.note: "He knew the tenses better than the teacher sometimes did."

questions.q: What did the teacher first think?
questions.note: "The teacher first thought he was shy."

questions.q: What did Baran say the real problem was?
options: He heard his own mistakes before speaking
He did not know the words
questions.note: "He could hear the mistakes in his own speech before the words left his mouth."

questions.q: What did the teacher change?
options: She used pairs instead of whole-class questions
questions.note: "She put students in pairs for five minutes at the start of every lesson."

questions.q: What happened to his writing?
options: It has not improved and nobody minds
questions.note: Son cümle.
